subject: Model Zeta: p95 Snapback — SLA Carveout Request & Traffic Plan
messages:
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>
To: Ryan Holt <ryan.holt@clearbank.com>, ops@clearbank.com
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Date: 2028-04-14T10:12:00-07:00
Subject: Model Zeta: p95 Snapback observed in canary — immediate guidance requested

Hi Ryan / ClearBank ops team,

Quick heads up: during the Zeta v2.4 canary (10% traffic, rolled at 09:00 PDT) we observed a p95 spike for your traffic from ~220ms to ~980ms starting at ~09:40 and stabilizing into bursts. This only affects traffic routed to Zeta v2.4; previous stable variant (v2.3) shows normal latency.

Attached: zeta-p95-telemetry-20280414.pdf with raw traces, and traffic-shift-playbook.md (playbook outlines our automated fallback steps).

We recommend two immediate actions — we need ClearBank sign-off to proceed:
- Option A (fast): shift your traffic back to Zeta v2.3 for all latency-sensitive endpoints (target 100% revert) — expected rollback completion in ~12–18 min once authorized.
- Option B (gradual): route 60% -> v2.3, keep 40% on v2.4 for continued signal collection; this reduces risk of regressions but keeps some telemetry.

If neither is acceptable, we can request a temporary SLA carveout for the window while we investigate root cause; that requires your written exception approval and Redwood exec concurrence.

Please confirm preferred path (A or B) and whether you authorize a temporary SLA tolerance for the next 48 hours while we run the root-cause analysis.

Apologies for the disruption — we are treating as P1 and have SRE on standby.

Thanks,
Vanessa Ortiz
Sr. Customer Reliability Manager
Redwood Inference

Attachments: zeta-p95-telemetry-20280414.pdf (report), traffic-shift-playbook.md (runbook)
From: Ryan Holt <ryan.holt@clearbank.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>
Cc: ops@clearbank.com
Date: 2028-04-14T10:28:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Model Zeta: p95 Snapback observed in canary — immediate guidance requested

Thanks Vanessa — appreciate the quick flag.

We need more detail before we sign off on a full revert. Two immediate asks:
1) Can you confirm whether the spike correlates with longer contexts or a specific kernel/quantization path?
2) If we approve Option A, what is the exact customer-visible window where SLAs could be breached? Our contract (Section 4.2) obligates Redwood to maintain p95 <= 300ms for latency-sensitive endpoints; we need a clear carveout form filled out if you require tolerance.

Please open an INC ticket (SRE + ClearBank ops) and share the INF ticket link. If you recommend an immediate partial shift to preserve telemetry, document the percentages and expected fallback timeline.

-Ryan
Director, Platform Engineering
ClearBank

On Apr 14, 2028, at 10:12 AM, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Quick heads up: during the Zeta v2.4 canary...
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>
To: ben_carter@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: 2028-04-14T10:45:00-07:00
Subject: INTERNAL: Authorization request — traffic-shift + SLA carveout form for ClearBank

Team — copying internal stakeholders. Summary: Zeta v2.4 canary produced p95 snapback on ClearBank traffic (details in attached PDF). ClearBank has requested more info but is open to Option A or B.

Recommended internal plan (we need approvals):
- Immediate action: authorize Ben to initiate an emergency traffic shift. Proposed default: Option A (full revert to v2.3) unless Ben requests partial (Option B) for signal reasons.
- Submit SLA exception form (attached sla-exception-form.pdf) to ClearBank for written carveout covering 2028-04-14T09:40:00Z to 2028-04-16T09:40:00Z (48h window).
- SRE runbook: energize INF-4512, attach daily telemetry snapshot for ClearBank.

Risk note: full revert reduces customer impact fastest. Partial keeps telemetry but prolongs exposure risk. Cost delta estimate for revert/fallback is minimal (no infra changes); main risk is potential customer credits if SLA breached without explicit carveout.

Please reply with Approve / Approve with conditions / Deny. I need a quick decision to avoid escalation.

Thanks,
Vanessa

On Apr 14, 2028 at 10:28 AM Ryan Holt <ryan.holt@clearbank.com> wrote:
> We need more detail before we sign off on a full revert...
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>, laura_bennett@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: 2028-04-14T10:58:00-07:00
Subject: Re: INTERNAL: Authorization request — traffic-shift + SLA carveout form for ClearBank

Approve to initiate emergency traffic shift. My ask:
- Execute Option A (100% revert to v2.3) now and hold until we have a root-cause postmortem.
- If ClearBank insists on telemetry, we can stand up a mirrored sampling (internal only) rather than exposing them to v2.4.
- Legal: do not sign any final SLA waiver that admits fault; only accept carveout language that is a mutual exception for a defined window.

Ben
VP, Customer Engineering
Redwood Inference

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>

Date: 2028-04-14T11:06:00-07:00
Subject: Re: INTERNAL: Authorization request — traffic-shift + SLA carveout form for ClearBank

Agree with Ben — approve full revert (Option A). A couple of operational asks:
- Notify Finance & CS to prepare potential credit calculations if the SLA is triggered.
- I will draft a short carveout note for the customer that takes neutral language ("mutual tolerance window for telemetry and remediation") and loop Legal for sign-off.
- Log the change in INF-4512 and link to the HubSpot deal so our renewal team is aware.

Laura Bennett
Head of Customer Success
Redwood Inference

On Apr 14, 2028 at 10:58 AM Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Approve to initiate emergency traffic shift...
From: Ryan Holt <ryan.holt@clearbank.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>, ops@clearbank.com
Date: 2028-04-18T16:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Model Zeta: p95 Snapback — SLA Carveout Request & Traffic Plan

Vanessa — thanks for the transparency and for moving quickly. ClearBank accepts Option A (full revert to v2.3) and will sign the mutual exception language you propose for the 48h window while you investigate.

Can you:
- Attach daily telemetry snapshots to INF-4512 by 09:00 PDT starting 2028-04-15 through 2028-04-17.
- Provide an RCA draft by 2028-04-20 COB.
- Confirm whether Redwood intends to offer any credit if postmortem indicates regression introduced by v2.4.

We are standing down from an escalation on our side as long as the revert is completed and we get the requested deliverables.

Thanks,
Ryan Holt
Director, Platform Engineering
ClearBank
